Fix the upstream Thermite dependency at one commit, record which commit and why that one, and build the toolchain from that pin. This is a trust-relevant input: the image's provenance is only as sharp as this pin.

```day-atom
{"in":["upstream-source"],"out":["pinned-dependency"],"next":["platform-fork"],"done":["upstream-pin"]}
```

T0 is blocked upstream. A struct with a field of user-declared type does not certify: the per-struct harness emits the field without weaving the referenced declaration, giving E0425 cannot find type. Primitive-only structs reach L3, so it is specific to user-declared field types.

G1 audit run: 257 BTreeMap call sites in the models, 150 covered by the shipped insert/get/contains_key/len surface, 107 not. get_mut (48) and entry (4) are read-modify-write idioms expressible as get+insert; is_empty is len==0; clear is Map::new(). Two genuine gaps remain.

G1 is remove (24 sites: frame 12, dma 4, irq 2, memory 2, smp 2, services 2) and iteration (25 sites: frame 10, memory 5, scheduler 4, smp 2, sync 2, services 2). Per tier: T1 needs neither and is cleared, T2 and T4 need both, T3 needs remove. Whether iteration is expressible under the Vec-of-pairs backing is upstream's design call.

G1 reported upstream as Thermite #123: Map needs remove (24 sites) and iteration (25 sites). The issue puts the design question to upstream rather than deciding it here — iteration may need no exec-position primitive if the spec surface can quantify over the map's domain, since every use we have is a fold or search whose contract is a forall.

Wrote src/context.th anyway while #122 is open. Eight of thirteen items certify at L3: all four enums, Registers, both spec fns, and create. create reaching L3 discharges P3, P4 and P5 for all inputs. Capability/UserContext/TrapFrame are L0 on G4; enter and resume are L0 on the non-scalar equivalence probe.

G4's scope is wider than reported: no declared type may appear inside any other declared type, in any position. Enum variants fail identically to struct fields, in both tuple and record form. The accurate statement is that the type graph must be one level deep.

Rung 1 is the largest capability jump per unit of work on the ladder: a recursive spec fn over an ADT has its declared bool return rewritten to nat, which blocks structural predicates. That is the difference between a kernel that can only build address spaces and one that can validate a page table it was handed.

Rung 3 is a multiplier rather than an adder: region-typed effects give race freedom syntactically, and DRF-SC then makes every sequential proof valid on multiple CPUs. It is the only rung whose check needs no solver and no new proof obligations.
